A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniAug study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and additional material in v3.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original UniAug benchmark results, scaling experiments and self-conditioning/guidance ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original benchmark outcomes, including five-shot classification, additional backbone comparisons and stratified data-scaling experiments.

M1.justification: The structure-only diffusion model, self-conditioning, denoising architecture and NOS guidance remain unchanged. The PIN and PolyGCL experiments apply the existing augmentor to additional downstream backbones without introducing a new augmentation procedure.

E1.justification: The pre-training sources and downstream datasets and prediction tasks are retained. Five-shot evaluation reuses Proteins and Enzymes; the other additions vary backbones or sampling within existing coverage. These are budget and configuration changes under E3.

E2.justification: v3 adds MVGRL, GRACE and BGRL, alongside a self-supervised GraphMAE evaluation, to link prediction and node classification comparisons (Tables 3–4). It also adds PIN and PolyGCL comparisons (Tables 15 and 21). The earlier pre-training comparisons remain in Tables 17 and 20.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include five-shot classification, self-supervised node embeddings with downstream heads, and PIN/PolyGCL backbones. Appendix D.4 adds pre-training on 25%, 50% and 75% subsets sampled within ten structural clusters to control data composition. The protocols for matched original experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of limited-label performance, dependence on downstream backbones, and data quantity separated more carefully from diversity (Tables 14–15 and 21; Figure 5). The original guidance, self-conditioning, homophily-disparity and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their mean/standard-deviation reporting and ten-fold, ten-run or ten-split conventions. The new checklist reiterates standard deviations across runs; it introduces no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial baseline, five-shot, backbone and stratified-scaling results. Table 14 reports 48.37 ± 4.77 five-shot accuracy on Enzymes; Table 21 shows UniAug–PolyGCL below PolyGCL on Texas, 86.70 versus 88.03. Original UniAug scores are retained. CFLP/Flickr is inconsistently reported as 0.00 ± 0.00 in Table 3 and OOM in retained Table 17.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Appendix A retain the same diffusion definitions, transition kernels, derivations and label-smoothing formula. Changes in mathematical display size and notation spacing introduce no new reasoning or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of a universal graph structure augmentor, cross-domain data scaling and plug-and-play benefits across node-, link- and graph-level tasks. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly acknowledges that SMALL/FULL/EXTRA vary in both quantity and diversity and interprets stratified sampling as evidence for quantity scaling. New passages discuss few-shot adaptability and backbone portability, explicitly noting PolyGCL improvements on three of four datasets. Existing limitations and broader-impact qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds the stratified-sampling recipe but drops the explicit best-of-three-backbone reporting disclosure. v2's direct public code URL is removed; v3's checklist instead states that code is in supplemental material. This changes access documentation without establishing actual resource availability. Most implementation details and hyperparameter grids are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MVGRL, GRACE, BGRL, GraphPrompt's few-shot protocol, PIN and PolyGCL. The existing related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose and section organization are retained, with localized baseline/results rewrites and expanded appendix explanations. Broader Impact moves from Appendix E to Section 6; acknowledgments, a disclaimer and the NeurIPS checklist are added, alongside author-affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially reorganized: v2 Tables 4–5 move to v3 Tables 17 and 20, while new grouped comparisons occupy main-text Tables 3–4. v3 adds five-shot/backbone tables and Figure 5, and resizes existing figures and tables. These are display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence for the central scaling and adaptability claims. Stratified sampling addresses the quantity/diversity confound in v2's scaling comparison, while additional self-supervised baselines, limited-label tests and backbone comparisons make validation more demanding and informative. These gains outweigh the limited reporting drawbacks of less direct code-access documentation and the inconsistent CFLP/Flickr entry.
